description: Blockchain Village focuses on smart contract vulnerability analysis, decentralized finance (DeFi) exploits, consensus protocol security, crypto wallet auditing, and blockchain node defense.

talks.title: Exploit Insecure Crypto Wallet (Presentation)
talks.teaser: Demonstrates vulnerability discovery and exploitation techniques targeting insecure cryptocurrency software wallets.
talks.summary:
Security researcher Peiyu Wang delivers an analysis of client-side vulnerability classes in cryptocurrency wallet applications in the Blockchain Village [00:04, 00:12]. Wang focuses on implementation and architectural flaws in desktop, web, and mobile wallet software rather than underlying blockchain consensus mechanisms [05:42].

The presentation explores session management flaws, demonstrating how missing cookie security attributes (such as HttpOnly and Secure flags) leave session tokens and credentials vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks [11:51]. Wang examines insecure Electron framework configurations in desktop wallets, illustrating how enabling nodeIntegration or utilizing deprecated Chromium runtimes allows malicious RPC payloads or web content to achieve full remote code execution on the host system [23:47].

talks.title: Is DeFi Ready for Prime Time? Q&A
talks.teaser: Ryan Rubin answers audience questions on decentralized finance architecture, systemic risks, and protocol auditing.
talks.summary:
In this interactive Q&A session from the DEF CON Safe Mode Blockchain Village, researchers and village organizers examine whether Decentralized Finance (DeFi) protocols and automated market makers are mature enough for enterprise financial adoption. Opening at 00:00, the panel explores the rapid influx of capital into decentralized lending pools and algorithmic trading platforms.

At 02:00, the discussion delves into smart contract composability vulnerabilities and flash loan exploitation, showing how economic dependencies across multiple smart contracts can lead to cascading liquidation failures.

Concluding at 05:00, the speakers address regulatory scrutiny, debating how emerging compliance mandates and centralized oversight interact with the core principles of censorship resistance and decentralized governance. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Securing the Cosmos
talks.teaser: Covers architectural security patterns, Tendermint consensus auditing, and threat vectors across the Cosmos blockchain ecosystem.
talks.summary:
Security engineer Ron Stoner presents an operational and defensive blueprint for architecting, deploying, and securing proof-of-stake validator nodes within the Cosmos blockchain ecosystem in the Blockchain Village [00:00, 10:16].

Stoner examines high-availability infrastructure design, analyzing single points of failure and recalling real-world lessons from power outages, ISP drops, and DDoS floods on unhedged consumer connections [20:36, 30:39]. He evaluates the security and performance trade-offs of bare-metal servers versus virtualized cloud instances [40:41], outlining sentry node network topologies, hardware security module (HSM) key isolation, and automated failover configurations designed to prevent catastrophic double-signing slashing events [30:46].

talks.title: Exploit Insecure Crypto Wallet (Stream Session)
talks.teaser: A live walkthrough demonstrating vulnerability identification, reverse engineering, and exploitation of flawed crypto wallet applications.
talks.summary:
In this hands-on exploitation demonstration from the DEF CON Safe Mode Blockchain Village, a security researcher walks through discovering and exploiting client-side vulnerabilities in cryptocurrency web and browser wallets. Opening at 00:04, the speaker introduces common architectural weaknesses in web-based cryptocurrency interfaces.

At 07:01, the presenter analyzes DOM-based message handling vulnerabilities, demonstrating how improper validation in window postMessage listeners allows malicious origins to inject unauthorized commands. At 14:01, the talk investigates stored cross-site scripting (XSS) bugs, showing that missing HTML output encoding allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript within the wallet's application context.

Moving to exploitation past 21:01 and 28:02, the researcher demonstrates how an attacker can leverage cross-site scripting to silently alter transaction recipients, manipulate approvals, and siphon cryptocurrency tokens directly from victims' wallets without triggering warning prompts. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: 7 Phases of Smart Contract Hacking
talks.teaser: Presents a structured seven-phase methodology for auditing and attacking smart contracts, from reconnaissance to post-exploitation.
talks.summary:
A smart contract security auditor presents a structured seven-phase methodology for evaluating, auditing, and exploiting decentralized applications on the Ethereum blockchain in the Blockchain Village [05:57]. The speaker emphasizes that smart contracts must be approached as autonomous, immutable software systems where standard post-deployment patch paradigms do not apply.

The presentation details each audit phase, contrasting automated static analysis tools with rigorous manual business logic verification to detect subtle algorithmic vulnerabilities [12:07, 12:15]. The speaker explores prominent attack classes—including reentrancy flaws, integer overflows, authorization bypasses, and front-running risks exacerbated by network congestion and mempool manipulation [18:23, 24:22]—providing actionable guidelines for developers to write defensive Solidity code and conduct thorough pre-deployment audits [30:32].
